Implementation of provisions of PESA
†*261. SHRI ALI ANWAR: Will the
Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that by
implementing provisions of the Panchayat
(Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act,
1996, the Dalits among Scheduled Tribes
have been deprived of their constitutional
right of reservation;
(b) if so, whether the matter has been
brought to the notice of Government; and
(c) whether Government would
consider the cancellation/amendment of
above Act?
Committee to look into demands of
Anganwadi Workers
*262. SHRI CHITTABRATA
MAJUMDAR:
SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND
CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether a committee has been
constituted by her Ministry as per the
direction of the Prime Minister to look into
and consider the demands of Anganwadi
Workers and Helpers;
(b) if so, the composition of the
committee and the terms and references
thereof; and
(c) the time-frame within which the
committee has to submit its report?
Educational backwardness among
minorities
†*263. SHRI PYARELAL
KHANDELWAL: Will the Minister of
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that one of the
main reasons of educational backwardness
of minorities, especially of the muslim
community is also the unscientific
education system of madrasas;
(b) whether it is also a fact that Maulana
Azad Foundation established to fulfil the
above purpose has also remained
unsuccessful in its objective;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

82
(c) if so, whether Government would
consider to adopt modern scientific method
in madrasas and minority institutions;
(d) if not, the details thereof; and
(e) the State-wise details of such
madrasas in the country which receive grant
and the manner of Government's control
over them?
Introduction of new elective subjects
*264. SHRI AMIR ALAM KHAN:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the CBSE
will introduce several new elective subjects
to students of class XI and XII, who wish
to break away from the regular subjects;
(b) if so, the details of those elective
subjects being offered to the students;
(c) whether the curriculum for elective
subjects in each discipline has been
developed and the schools have been
informed about the introduction of the
subjects; and
(d) the steps his Ministry would take
to tackle the problem of shortage of teachers
for teaching these subjects?
Remuneration to Anganwadi Workers
and Helpers
*265. SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
SHRI CHITTABRATA
MAJUMDAR:
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND
CHILD DEVELOPMENT  be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the Integrated Child
Development Scheme is a Central
Government Scheme;
(b) the remuneration paid to the
Anganwadi Workers and Helpers by
Government;
(c) whether Government have received
any representation for increasing the
remuneration of Anganwadi Workers and
Helpers;
(d) whether it is the policy of
Government to 'retire' Anganwadi Workers
and Helpers who have reached 58 years of
age;
(e) if so, whether the retired Anganwadi
Workers and Helpers are being provided
with any pension or gratuity;
(f) if so, the details thereof; and
(g) if not, the reasons therefor?
Popularisation of coconut water
*266. PROF. P.J. KURIEN: Will the
Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are considering
to popularise coconut water as a natural
healthy drink in place of other artificial soft
drinks;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government have received
any proposal in this regard;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) the action taken by Government in
this regard?

83
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Special Scheme for education of
dalits
†*267. SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS
BAL APTE:
SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that with a view
to impart better education to dalits of the
entire country Government are preparing a
special scheme;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government have held any
discussion with various State Governments
in this regard;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) Government's contribution in the
above scheme and the extent of it?
Shortage of electricity in
Maharashtra
*268. SHRI TARIQ ANWAR: Will the
Minister of POWER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is acute
shortage of electricity in Maharashtra;
(b) if so, the quantum of load shedding;
and
(c) the possible steps/solutions the
State and Central Governments are taking
in this regard?
Rural electrification targets in Tenth
Five Year Plan
†*269. SHRI SURENDRA LATH: Will
the Minister of POWER be pleased to state:
(a) the target laid down for rural
electrification in the Tenth Five Year Plan
and the target achieved so far;
(b) whether it is a fact that in some
States 80 per cent houses have no
accessibility of electricity as on date;
(c) the funds allocated to different
States for rural electrification in the Tenth
Five Year Plan; and
(d) the funds utilised out of the funds
allocated to different States?
Kendriya Vidyalayas in KBK region
*270. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to sanction
five Kendriya Vidyalayas for the KBK
region in Orissa;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also proposed to set
up a centrally funded institution of higher
education in this most backward tribal-
dominated region of the country; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?
Website for Central Acts
*271. DR. PRABHA THAKUR:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of LAW AND
JUSTICE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have made a
net-version of the Ministry-wise
compilation of all the Acts of Parliament
along with detailed text and rules made
thereunder, for the free access of general
public;

84
(b) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor; and
(c) whether Government will consider
creating such a website of Acts of
Parliament along with their updated text
and rules framed thereunder?
Action plan for food processing
industries
*272. SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL:
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have finalized
vision strategy and action plan for food
processing industries in the country till date;
(b) if so, the details thereof and
budgetary allocations made therefor during
2006-07, State-wise; and
(c) the steps taken so far to give effect
to the vision particularly in the State of
Rajasthan?
Continuing Education Programme
†*273. MISS ANUSUIYA UIKEY: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the number of districts where
Continuing Education Programme (Satat
Shiksha Karyakram) has been introduced,
State-wise;
(b) the district-wise and year-wise
details of the amount sanctioned and the
number of instalments released for this
purpose; and
(c) the time taken for release of second
instalment after first instalment and the
criteria adopted in this regard?
Private hydro power projects
†*274. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there are
certain projects in hydel power generation
sector in the country generating less power
than their capacity;
(b) if so, the facts in this regard;
(c) whether Government have
formulated such projects for hydel power
generation where private sector has been
assigned responsibility of construction;
and
(d) if so, the projects under construction
by private sector in hydel power sector?
Payment of incorrect salary to
teachers
†*275. SHRI UDAY PRATAP
SINGH: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether instances of forcing of
public school teachers by school
administrators to sign on inflated salary
has come to the notice of Government;
(b) if so, the action being taken by
Government against these schools; and
(c) the rules laid down to give full salary
to teachers appointed in these schools, as
per their qualifications?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

85
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Lacunae in the Persons with
Disabilities Act
*276. SHRI C. PERUMAL: Will the
Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE AND
EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether there are numerous lacunae
in the Persons with Disabilities Act, 1995
especially with the definition clause; and
(b) if so, the action taken to rectify the
lacunae?
Schools without buildings
†*277. SHRI MOTILAL VORA: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the number of primary schools and
middle schools running in tents and under
trees;
(b) whether it is possible to get
education in the summer, winter and rainy
season in such conditions;
(c) whether this is also a reason for
decrease in the number of students in
schools;
(d) what should be the maximum
distance between two primary schools;
(e) whether this rule is being followed;
and
(f) the steps being taken by Government
to provide permanent buildings and basic
amenities to primary and middle schools?
Grants for flour mills and rice mills
in J&K
*278. SHRI T.S. BAJWA: Will the
Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether his Ministry have any
proposal under the consideration to restart
the grant-in-aid for flour mills and rice mills,
particularly to Jammu and Kashmir as it is
a militancy affected State;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and
(d) the details of grant given to Jammu
and Kashmir during the years 2002—06,
year-wise?
Renovation of Barauni and Kanti
Thermal Power Stations
†*279. SHRI MAHENDRA SAHNI:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government propose to
renovate the Barauni and Kanti Thermal
Power Stations;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and
(d) the details of the proposal relating
to the extent of augmentation in power
generation capacity after renovation of
these plants and the amount allotted for
this purpose?
Professional institutes providing
higher education
*280. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY:
SHRI PRAVEEN
RASHTRAPAL:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of professional institutes,
imparting higher education in technology,
engineering, architecture, agriculture,
management, etc. in the country; separately
in private (aided and unaided) and

86
Government sector, seat capacity, State-
wise;
(b) whether reservation of seats for SC/
ST and OBCs is not available in unaided
private professional institutes;
(c) if so, details thereof;
(d) whether Government proposes to
amend the Constitution of India to provide
for such reservation; and
(e) if so, details, thereof and if not, the
reasons therefor?

List of Questions for WRITTEN ANSWERS

Development; Law and Justice; Mines; Minority Affairs; New and Renewable

Canned milk for children
†1949. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will
the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that several
companies in the country are making
canned milk for children by violating the
rules and regulations;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the
Bureau of Indian Standards has formulated
norms for the production of 109 highly-
sensitive items, but there are 34 items for
which license is not compulsory for a
company;
(c) if so, whether sub-standard items
are being produced for want of proper
arrangement for testing quality of such
products; and
(d) the steps being taken by
Government to check production of these
sub-standard products?
Food Processing units in Rajasthan
1950. DR. ABHISHEK MANU
SINGHVI: Will the Minister of FOOD
PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) the food processing units sanctioned
in Rajasthan during the last three years;
(b) the food items processed therein;
and
(c) the steps being taken to revive the
units that have been closed down?
Survey for utilization of fruits and
vegetables in NER
1951. SHRI KARNENDU
BHATTACHARJEE: Will the Minister of
FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be
pleased to state:
(a) whether any survey has been carried
out by Government for utilization of fruits
and vegetables for processing in the North
Eastern States, particularly in Assam;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the details of assistance, if any, given
by way of cold storage, food testing etc. to
State/private entrepreneurs; and
(d) whether any funds have been granted
by Government for setting up food
processing industries in the North-East
Zone, particularly in Assam?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

445
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
FDI in food processing sector
1952. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA: Will the Minister of FOOD
PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether a section of agro-based food
processing companies have been given
approval for 100 per cent FDI but the
industry in general has expressed its
reservations;
(b) if so, whether Government have
taken any decision to enact a legislation in
this regard; and
(c) if not, what are the main reasons for
delay and by what time, a final decision for
introducing the legislation would be taken?
New projects/units for food
processing
1953. SHRI PRAVEEN
RASHTRAPAL: Will the Minister of
FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be
pleased to state:
(a) whether many new projects/units
have been established during the last five
years;
(b) if so, the details thereof year-wise
and State-wise with the sanction and help
of Government;
(c) when the last survey was conducted
in the State of Gujarat for food processing
units; and
(d) the details of survey and utilization
of the information so gained?
Special food processing zones
†1954. SHRI SHAHID SIDDIQUI:
Will the Minister of  FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) the number of Special Zones set up
by his Ministry in Uttar Pradesh till now;
and
(b) the steps taken for the food
processing of fruits and vegetables in Uttar
Pradesh and the schemes launched so far
and the details thereof?
New technology to teachers
1955. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have taken any
new initiatives for making teachers aware
of new technology by providing them all
latest technical support and guidance; and
(b) if so, the details thereof and the steps
taken or proposed to be taken for making
available quality and fruitful education to
the students in the next five years?
Scholarship to post-matric students in
Andhra Pradesh
1956. SHRI NANDI YELLAIAH: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the details of funds sought by Andhra
Pradesh State Government for the post
matric scholarship in the current financial
year 2006-07;
(b) the amount released to Andhra
Pradesh Government so far;
(c) the number of students benefited by
such scholarships during 2005-06, and of
those proposed to be benefited in the current
year; and
(d) the amount and percentage of
contribution of Andhra Pradesh
Government in post-matric scholarship as
its committed liability?

446
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Suggestions for States in reservation
†1957. SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
 SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have sought suggestions from State
Governments with regard to introduction
of reserved seats for backward classes in
the field of higher education from academic
session of 2007;
(b) if so, the facts thereof;
(c) when the suggestions were sought
by Government and whether a deadline was
set for State Government to give
suggestions; and
(d) the names of the States which had
already sent their suggestions to
Government by October, 2006 along with
the details of the suggestions?
First-aid facilities in Government
schools
1958. SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that First-aid
facilities for school children are not available
in most of the Government schools
particularly in Primary and Middle
Government Schools situated in rural areas
of the country;
(b) if so, the details of specific reasons
therefor;
(c) whether Government have
formulated any scheme and programme on
the pattern of public schools to provide
first-aid facilities to the students in
Government schools;
(d) if so, the steps taken or proposed to
be taken by Government to implement the
above scheme in the interest of students;
and
(e) if not, what is the reaction of
Government thereto?
Revision of guidelines for Mid-day
meal Scheme
1959. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA : Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have revised the guidelines of the mid-day
meal scheme;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is a fact that the existing
nutritional norms were found to be
inadequate to address the growing needs of
children; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Fee structure of professional
colleges
1960. SHRI MATILAL SARKAR: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
the professional colleges under private
management are charging, officially or non-
officially, large amount of money for
admitting students in some attractive
courses of studies;
(b) whether Government have any plan
to increase the number of seats and also the
number of professional colleges to cater
the needs to a greater possible extent; and
(c) the programme of Government in
detail to save the deserving students from
the hands of the education-marketeers?

447
Fake NRIs seeking admission
1961. SHRIMATI VIPLOVE
THAKUR : Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the fact that students from well-off families
posing themselves as NRI are getting
admission in engineering colleges and
management institutes on payment of huge
amount in various States of the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof and
Government's reaction thereto;
(c) whether Government have
conducted an enquiry in this regard;
(d) if so, the details thereof and the action
taken/likely to be taken by Government
against such students and colleges/
institutes; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Financial responsibility under Right
to Education Act
1962. SHRI MOINUL HASSAN: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Right to Education Act,
2005 provide for Central Government's
responsibility of financial assistance to
State Governments, technical resource
support to the State Governments,
monitoring progress of implementation and
appropriate steps in case of default;
(b) if so, whether all these provisions
have been dropped altogether in the Model
Bill, 2006; and
(c) if so, the reasons therefor?
Mid-day meal scheme
1963. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that certain
category of school children are provided
mid-day meal at school;
(b) if so, the details with allocation made,
spent and the number of beneficiary
children, during the last three years, year-
wise and State-wise;
(c) whether it is a fact that there are
reports of such meal being of poor quality
and prepared in unhygienic conditions;
(d) if so, the details thereof;
(e) whether Government are considering
to allow reputed fast food manufacturers
to take over the mid-day meal scheme; and
(f) if so, the details with reaction of the
industry to the proposal?
Enquiry against Vice Chancellor of
MGIHU
†1964. SHRI DHARAM PAL
SABHARWAL: Will the Minister of
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Committee constituted
to enquire into serious offences against Vice-
Chancellor of Mahatama Gandhi
International Hindi University of Vardha
has submitted its report to Government;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government have studied
this report; and
(d) if so, the status of action taken in
this regard?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

448
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Extension of secondary education
in Madhya Pradesh and
Chhattisgarh
†1965. SHRI PYARELAL
KHANDELWAL: Will the Minister of
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether any Central scheme for
extension of secondary education for
Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh is under
consideration of Government;
(b) whether Governments of these
States have submitted any schemes to the
Central Government in this regard; and
(c) if so, the reaction of Government in
this regard?
Review of vocational education
programme
1966. SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether National Working Group
on vocationalisation of education has
reviewed vocational education programme;
(b) if so, the details thereof alongwith
the recommendations of the said group;
(c) whether Government have issued
instructions to the State Governments to
implement these recommendations;
(d) if so, the details thereof;
(e) whether the combination of the
subjects available at senior secondary level
do not match with the subjects available
for higher education; and
(f) if so, the remedial steps taken by
Government to ensure that the students
are not deprived of taking admission for
higher education?
Suicide of students
†1967. SHRI SURENDRA LATH: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the number of children who
committed suicide in various parts of the
country after the results of C.B.S.E.
examinations;
(b) whether Government would take
any steps to remove their depression;
(c) whether it is also a fact that not only
weak students but also brilliant students
have committed suicide; and
(d) whether Government are
contemplating to recruit consultants/
advisors in the schools?
Students in science education
†1968. SHRI MANGANI LAL
MANDAL: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that students in
the country are losing their interest and
inclination towards science education, day-
by-day;
(b) whether it is also a fact that
Government have received a representation
from Rao Committee in this regard;
(c) whether it is a fact that in order to
face the challenges in future, the need to
increase ten times the existing availability
of eminent researchers and Ph.D. degree
holders as well as engineers having the
degree of Ph.D. is being stressed upon;
(d) whether it is a fact that the
Committee constituted for this purpose
under the Chairmanship of Prof. M.M.
Sharma has submitted its recommendations
to Government; and

449
(e) if so, the details thereof and
Government's view in this regard?
Recognition of colleges and courses by
NCTE
1969. SHRI KESHUBHAI S. PATEL:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that National
Council of Teachers' Education (NCTE) is
giving recognition to B.Ed. colleges, even
though the concerned State Government
has not given no objection certificate;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether it is a fact that National
Council of Teachers' Education (NCTE) is
not approving M.Ed. courses, even though
the concerned State Government has given
no objection certificate; and
(d) if so, the reasons therefor?
Violence and indiscipline in
campuses
1970. SHRI SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
SHRI O.T. LEPCHA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have taken
cognizance of growing cases of violence and
indiscipline in the campuses;
(b) whether Government have taken a
view on the recommendations of the
Lyngdoh Committee on the elections of the
student's union; and
(c) if so the details of the steps
being taken to implement the
recommendations?
Vocational education in rural and
urban areas
†1971. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that only 3 per
cent of students in rural areas and 6 per
cent of boys in urban areas are getting
vocational education in the country;
(b) if not, the facts thereof;
(c) whether it is a fact that the above
percentage in other countries in the world
is more than that of India; and
(d) if so, the average percentage of
students getting vocational education at
international level?
Percentage of students in higher
education
†1972. SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that only 10 per
cent of students are getting education in
the universities in the country while this
percentage is 20 to 25 per cent in other
developing countries;
(b) if so, the facts thereof in this regard;
(c) whether Government have
submitted any plan to the Planning
Commission for expansion of higher
education during the Eleventh Five Year
Plan; and
(d) if so, its draft thereof?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

450
Negative points in reduction of
illiterates
1973. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
